2409.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aiweí, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eyu- (“lifetime; long time”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ey- (“vital energy; life”). Equivalent to the locative case of αἰών (aiṓn), with or without -ν (-n).

2491.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰewdʰ-. Cognates include Sanskrit बोधति (bodhati), Gothic 𐌰𐌽𐌰𐌱𐌹𐌿𐌳𐌰𐌽 (anabiudan), and Old English bēodan (English bede, bid).

2496.t: From σείω (seíō, “to shake”) + -μός (-mós). The "earthquake" sense is an ellipsis of γῆς σεισμός (gês seismós, “shaking of the earth”).

2454.t: From δια- (dia-, “through, between”) + φέρω (phérō, “to bring, carry”).

2431.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sérpeti. Cognates include Sanskrit सर्पति (sarpati, “to glide, crawl”), and Latin serpō (“to creep, crawl”).

2495.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷóteros, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷóteros, from *kʷos (“which”) + *-teros (contrastive suffix).

2467.t: Of loanword origin, probably from a Mediterranean Pre-Greek language; compare Hebrew כּוֺפֶר /כֹּפֶר (kōp̱er, “pitch, tar; henna”), Aramaic כּוּפְרָא / ܟܘܦܪܐ (kūp̄rā, “pitch, tar; henna”), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎔𐎗 (kpr, “henna”), Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀞𐀫 (ku-pa-ro,…

2414.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂ep Proto-Indo-European *-o Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó Proto-Hellenic *apó Ancient Greek ἀπό (ăpó) Ancient Greek ἀπο- (ăpo-) Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- Proto-Indo-European *dʰédʰeh₁ti Ancient Greek τίθημι (títhēmi)…

2494.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷotsos, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷóti, adverb from *kʷos (“what”). Compare the indefinite form ποσός (posós).

2418.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂léh₁wr̥. Cognate with Old Armenian ալեւր (alewr).

2479.t: From πάνοπλος (pánoplos, “in full armour”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from πᾶς (pâs, “all, every”) + ὅπλον (hóplon, “armour”).

2438.t: From Proto-Indo-European *webʰ- (“to weave”), and therefore related distantly to Old English wefan (whence English weave), Sanskrit उ॒भ्नाति॑ (ubhnā́ti, “entwine”), Persian بافتن (bâftan), Tocharian A wäp- (“weave”).

2451.t: From διακόπτω (diakóptō, “to cut in two, cut through”) + -ή (-ḗ). By surface analysis, δια- (dia-, “dia-, through-”) + κοπή (kopḗ, “cutting in pieces”).

2478.t: Probably an enlargement in -τάζω (-tázō) of a Proto-Indo-European *snewd- (“to slumber, doze”); for the formation, compare κλαστάζω (klastázō) and βαστάζω (bastázō, “to lift up”).

2407.t: Seemingly, a formation with the suffix -λός (-lós) like στρεβλός (streblós) and τυφλός (tuphlós), but without obvious etymology.

2457.t: From εἰ (ei, “if”) and root of τά (tá).

2447.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *dn̥s-, zero-grade of *dens- (“thick, dense”), and cognate with Latin dēnsus (“dense”), Hittite [script needed] (daššu-, “heavy, strong”), though this depends on whether *-n̥s- does yield *-σ- (*-s-) in Greek.

2406.t: From the root of χράομαι (khráomai, “to use, desire”) + -ιμος (-imos, “-able, -like”).

2430.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hélos, from Proto-Indo-European *sélos ~ *séles- (“marsh”). Cognate with Sanskrit सरस् (sáras) and perhaps Old Armenian եղտիւր (ełtiwr).

2402.t: From φάρμακον (phármakon, “herb, drug”). The noun only in biblical Greek, for φαρμακεύς (pharmakeús).

2424.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁elh₂- (“to drive somewhere”), albeit with no certain cognates.

2472.t: Deverbative of μέριμνα (mérimna, “anxiety, concern”). Cognates include Latin memor and Sanskrit स्मरति (smarati, “to think, to recollect”)

2460.t: From Proto-Indo-European *yéwgos (“team of yoked animals”). See also ζεύγνυμι (zeúgnumi, “to join”).

2493.t: By surface analysis, πέσσω (péssō, “to cook, to bake”) + -μα (-ma). According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *pékʷ-mn̥, itself from *pekʷ-.

2405.t: From χόρτος (khórtos, “fodder”) + -άζω (-ázō, suffix to form a verb).

2487.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pṓds. Cognates include Mycenaean Greek 𐀡 (po) (dat. 𐀡𐀆 (po-de /⁠podei⁠/)), Latin pēs, Sanskrit पद् (pad), Old Armenian ոտն (otn) and հետ (het), Gothic 𐍆𐍉𐍄𐌿𐍃 (fōtus) and Old English fōt (English foot).

2464.t: From καταλύω (katalúō, “stay over night”) + -μα (-ma, “a suffix forming neuter nouns denoting the effect or result of an action a particular instance of an action, or the object of an action”)

2455.t: From reanalysis of older δρεπάνη f (drepắnē) as neuter, originally formed as δρέπω (drépō, “to pluck; to cut off”) + -άνη (-ắnē, instrument noun suffix).

2458.t: From εὐθηνός (euthēnós) + -έω (-éō). Variant form of εὐθενέω (euthenéō, “to thrive, flourish”).

2474.t: From μόσχος (móskhos, “calf; young bull”) + -άριον (-ắrĭon, diminutive suffix).

2415.t: From ἀποκρίνω (apokrī́nō, “to separate”) + -σις (-sĭs) and ἀπο- (apo-, “from, off”) + κρίσις (krísis, “decision”).

2483.t: From πεντήκοντα (pentḗkonta) + ἀρχός (arkhós), literally “commander of fifty”.
